extracted.intended_audience: Developers and contributors to the SageMath codebase and documentation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for writing, testing, linting, and documenting code and objects in the SageMath project (Python/Cython), including devcontainer usage, CI-local tooling, and documentation conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docker image naming and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Images with specific suffixes denote particular build stages and contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: suffix -with-targets-optional: full builds + make ptest logs + source tree; -with-system-packages: system installation with system packages, no source tree; -configured: partial source tree and configure finished; -with-targets-pre: partial source tree with full installation of non-Python packages; -with-targets: full source tree and full installation but make ptest not run. Note some images may be outdated due to build errors; standard and minimal images discontinued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use VS Code Dev Containers for development
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the VS Code Dev Containers extension to develop inside prebuilt Docker dev containers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Install 'Dev Containers' extension, use provided sample devcontainer.json files in $SAGE_ROOT/.devcontainer/*, open folder in container (Reopen Folder in Container), or use 'Dev Containers: Open Folder in Container'. Choose appropriate devcontainer (e.g. ubuntu-jammy-standard). See 'onCreateCommand' and 'updateContentCommand' logs to understand install/bootstrap steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dev container side-effect caution (symlinks and scripts)
rubrics_metrics.description: After configuring and using the dev container, certain files are symlinks that work only inside the container.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files like $SAGE_ROOT/venv, $SAGE_ROOT/prefix, and (possibly) $SAGE_ROOT/logs will be symlinks valid only inside the container; $SAGE_ROOT/sage script will not work locally. After using the dev container, remove logs if they are symlinks and rerun the configure script in the local environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain uv.lock for reproducible dependencies
rubrics_metrics.description: uv.lock captures exact package versions for all systems to ensure consistent, reproducible installations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: uv.lock is automatically updated during uv operations (uv add, uv run) and periodically by Renovate. Manually update with 'uv lock -U' when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tox as the standard entry point for testing and linting
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage includes a tox configuration (SAGE_ROOT/src/tox.ini) used for portability testing, modularized distributions, and library testing/linting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invoke via './sage --tox' (or 'tox' if tox is in system). The tox configuration exposes named 'tox environments' (doctest, coverage, startuptime, pycodestyle-minimal, relint, codespell, rst, ruff-minimal, etc.). Use '-e <envlist>' to run specific environments and '--help' for options (e.g. -p auto for parallel).

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctest environment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The doctest tox environment runs Sage's doctester and requires that Sage has already been built.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invoke with './sage -tox -e doctest' or './sage -t'. A tox virtual environment is created but Sage is invoked in the normal Sage environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage (doctest under Coverage.py)
rubrics_metrics.description: Run doctests under Coverage.py to measure coverage and optionally generate HTML reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use './sage -tox -e coverage.py' for coverage and './sage -tox -e coverage.py-html' for HTML reports. Coverage environments require Sage to be built; a virtualenv is created but coverage is executed with Sage in the normal environment. See [coverage:run] configuration in SAGE_ROOT/src/tox.ini.

rubrics_metrics.name: coverage (ensure functions have doctests)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'coverage' environment checks that each function has at least one doctest (typically in EXAMPLES or TESTS blocks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run './sage -tox -e coverage' (equivalent to './sage --coverageall') for a summary; pass file/directory args for detailed reports. Documentation: coverage.readthedocs.io.

rubrics_metrics.name: startuptime measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure time to load components during Sage startup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run './sage -tox -e startuptime' (equivalent to './sage --startuptime'). Without args it gives modules sorted by contribution to startup time; with args it gives details for specific modules/files.

rubrics_metrics.name: pycodestyle-minimal as baseline style check
rubrics_metrics.description: A minimal pycodestyle configuration is defined; as of Sage 9.5 the whole library conforms to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run './sage -tox -e pycodestyle-minimal -- src/sage/' to verify. Developers preparing a branch for a Sage ticket should ensure this passes.

rubrics_metrics.name: pycodestyle (thorough style check) and PR guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: A more thorough pycodestyle configuration checks full PEP8/pycodestyle rules; new code in PRs should not introduce warnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing a PR that adds new code, verify './sage -tox -e pycodestyle' does not issue warnings for the added code to avoid later cleanup PRs. Avoid mixing coding-style fixes with productive changes in the same PR because it makes review harder. Use '--count -qq' to reduce output to counts only for planning clean-up work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ruff linting configurations
rubrics_metrics.description: Ruff is used with two configurations: ruff-minimal (baseline) and ruff (thorough).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As of Sage 10.3 the library conforms to ruff-minimal; developers should verify './sage -tox -e ruff-minimal' passes. For PRs that add new code, ensure './sage -tox -e ruff' emits no warnings for the added code. Same anti-pattern advice: don't mix style fixes and functional changes in same PR.

rubrics_metrics.name: relint forbidden-pattern checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Relint checks all source files for forbidden text patterns defined by regular expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relint flags outdated Python constructions, plain TeX commands when LaTeX alternatives exist, common doc markup mistakes, and modularization anti-patterns. Configuration at SAGE_ROOT/src/.relint.yml.

rubrics_metrics.name: codespell for misspellings
rubrics_metrics.description: Use codespell to check for misspelled words in source code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run './sage -tox -e codespell -- <path>' and configure skips and dictionaries via SAGE_ROOT/src/.codespell-dictionary.txt and SAGE_ROOT/src/.codespell-ignore.txt. The codespell invocation in Sage skips many binary and doc formats and language doc directories; errors can cause non-zero exit codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cython-lint for Cython files
rubrics_metrics.description: Use cython-lint to check coding style in Cython sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invoke via the corresponding tox environment; ensures Cython files meet project style expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pytest use and invocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Pytest is available but used only in limited parts of Sage; can run tests in parallel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Install via './sage -i pytest pytest_xdist'. Usage: './sage -pytest path/to/test_file.py' or './sage -pytest' to run all tests. Use '-n' to run tests in parallel (e.g. '-n 4' or '-n auto'). VS Code integration via the Python extension. Configuration: SAGE_ROOT/conftest.py.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pyright for static typing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Pyright as the static type checker for Python code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Install manually via 'npm install -g pyright'. Usage: './sage -tox -e pyright path/to/file.py' or 'pyright path/to/file.py'. Checking whole library may need increased Node memory: NODE_OPTIONS='--max-old-space-size=8192' pyright. VS Code: use Pylance extension. Configuration: SAGE_ROOT/pyrightconfig.json.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pyflakes for common error checking
rubrics_metrics.description: Pyflakes checks for common coding errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run via the relevant tox environment or local pyflakes invocation as part of linting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use act to run GitHub Actions locally
rubrics_metrics.description: act (or 'gh act') can run GitHub Actions locally using Docker to speed up development of Actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Install via gh extension facility (gh extension install https://github.com/nektos/gh-act) or standalone act. Use 'gh act -l' to list actions, 'gh act -j <job>' to run a job. act can cache pulled data to speed repeated runs; flags like '-p false' (use already pulled images) and '-r' (do not remove images after run) control behavior. See act documentation for extra Docker configuration steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation is ReST + Sphinx and build process
rubrics_metrics.description: Sage manuals are written in reStructuredText and built with Sphinx via the 'sage --docbuild' wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts located under SAGE_ROOT/src/doc/en/<manual>. Build with 'sage --docbuild <document-name> <format>' (e.g. 'sage --docbuild tutorial html' or 'sage --docbuild reference html'). Use 'sage --docbuild -h' or '-H' for help. To see changes in reference manual (generated from source), build Sage ('sage -b') then 'sage --docbuild reference html'. Output formats supported by Sphinx (pdf, html, etc.) can be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Run doctests and tests on documentation changes
rubrics_metrics.description: All documentation files must pass tests (doctests) after modification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After editing docs, run 'sage -tp SAGE_ROOT/src/doc/en/tutorial/' or the appropriate doctest invocation. The 'coverage'/doctest tox environments discussed earlier apply when testing docs too.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sphinx cross-referencing and link roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Use appropriate Sphinx roles (:mod:, :class:, :meth:, :func:, etc.) for cross-references; Sage also defines custom roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ':mod:`sage.module_name`', ':func:`~sage.mod1.mod2.func1`' (short link using ~). Local names allowed for linking methods within the same class. Intersphinx can reference other packages; Sage-specific roles include :issue:, :sage_root:, :wikipedia:, :arxiv:, :oeis:, :doi:, :mathscinet:, and many package/library-specific roles. Use './sage -python -m sphinx.ext.intersphinx src/doc/common/_vendor/numpy.inv' to inspect available cross references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymous hyperlinks to avoid duplicate targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Use anonymous hyperlinks (two underscores) to avoid duplicate explicit target name errors in Sphinx pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using a single underscore creates an explicit target name and must be unique in the page; using two underscores (..) creates anonymous targets that avoid the 'Duplicate explicit target name' warning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report broken links with --warn-links
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the '--warn-links' flag when building documentation to report broken links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Sphinx will not rebuild a document that hasn't been updated, so it may not report broken links in unchanged files. Example: 'sage --docbuild --warn-links reference html'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include new modules in the reference manual index
rubrics_metrics.description: To have a new file appear in the reference manual, add it to the appropriate index file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add the new file name to SAGE_ROOT/src/doc/en/reference/<module>/index.rst. For files under combinat/, add the file to the package __init__.py index and to SAGE_ROOT/src/doc/en/reference/combinat/module_list.rst.

rubrics_metrics.name: Python language version and backports policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow the time-window-based support policy for minimum supported Python versions; features must be available in that version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum supported Python version is declared in pyproject.toml. Backports are allowed via: 'from __future__ import annotations' to modernize annotations per PEP 563 (include this import for code using annotations), and via typing_extensions package which is declared as a dependency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design to fit the Sage class hierarchy
rubrics_metrics.description: When adding new functionality, design classes and objects to integrate with existing Sage structures and hierarchies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., implement elements of a ring by deriving from sage.structure.element.RingElement rather than creating unrelated classes. Think about how new code fits with other Sage code and structure to promote reuse and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sage special methods and naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Naming conventions: Python predefined special methods use double leading+trailing underscores (__XXX__), Sage-defined special methods use leading+trailing single underscores (_XXX_), single leading underscore = semi-private, double leading underscore = really private.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sage special methods are typically _XXX_. Eventually trailing underscores will be used consistently. Implement required special methods appropriate to the object (e.g., _latex_, _repr_, others depending on object nature).

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement LaTeX representation for objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Sage object should support latex(x) by implementing a _latex_ method returning a LaTeX representation suitable for math mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define _latex_(self) returning LaTeX that can be typeset within math mode (do not include $ delimiters). When typesetting components, call latex(c) rather than c._latex_() to handle cases where c may not implement _latex_. Include a docstring and an example demonstrating LaTeX generation. Allowed macros: those from amsmath, amssymb, amsfonts, or macros defined in sage.misc.latex_macros.
